study: Frozen Prop Candidate Scaling and Survival Study v1
purpose: Estimate payout, breach, and drawdown-utilization frontiers without changing or selecting strategy signals.

candidateSet.label: DM Optimized 63D/Daily
candidateSet.status: historically selected development candidate; forward paper test remains authoritative

selectionRule: Report the complete frontier. Do not promote the scale with the highest historical expected payout as optimal.

execution.observedFillCalibration: Apply only to DM Optimized when the stored broker sample is calibrated; do not transfer small-cap execution observations to Dow controls.
execution.partialFillTreatment: Scale DM Optimized market exposure by the observed aggregate mean fill ratio and disclose this as an approximation, not an order-level replay. Other candidates retain full-fill backtest assumptions until candidate-specific observations exist.

intradayRule.historicalTreatment: Use a conservative daily-OHLC envelope formed from held securities' lows/highs. Because daily bars do not reveal cross-security simultaneity or high/low ordering, both static and especially trailing results remain approximate.
intradayRule.trailingOrderingSensitivity: Assume session high precedes session low when testing the trailing floor; label this conservative ordering sensitivity.
intradayRule.forwardRequirement: Persist intraday account equity marks for DM Optimized 63D/Daily; replace the proxy only prospectively, never rewrite historical forward records.

outputs: expected net payout after challenge/reset fees
median time to first payout conditional on payout
interpretationGuards: No strategy signal, universe, lookback, cadence, or overlay weight may be changed by this study.
DM Optimized historical results are selection-contaminated and cannot substitute for forward paper evidence.
Five years of Dow history and one year of optimized-candidate history do not support long-history regime claims.
Daily OHLC breach estimates are approximate until genuine intraday account marks exist.
No scale is called optimal from this historical simulation.
